parsed.summary: This paper proposes a channel-aware framework for selecting OR-folded Bloom filter representations based on time-varying communication conditions. Using two phishing URL datasets, the authors evaluate the approach under three channel models and demonstrate that it improves communication efficiency and receiver freshness compared to complete-filter and lossless-compression baselines.

chk_problem.value: Periodic transmission of Bloom filters in communication-constrained distributed systems can cause substantial overhead and stale receiver states when channel conditions vary.
chk_problem.paper_quote: Periodic Bloom-filter transmission can impose substantial overhead in communication-constrained distributed systems.

chk_method.value: An online policy that selects the largest FPR-qualified OR-folded Bloom filter representation from a catalog of fine-grained folded views based on time-varying communication conditions.
chk_method.paper_quote: The sender retains an unchanged canonical filter, constructs a catalog satisfying a maximum FPR, and selects the FPR-qualified representation with the largest retained length supported by the communication resources available at each reporting opportunity.

chk_data.value: The PhiUSIIL and URL-Phish datasets, using 5,000 malicious URLs for insertion and 50,000 disjoint benign URLs for absent queries.
chk_data.paper_quote: The PhiUSIIL [14] and URL-Phish [15] datasets are evaluated using 5,000 malicious URLs for insertion and 50,000 disjoint benign URLs as absent queries.

chk_setup.value: Evaluation using 20 repetitions of 500 transmission opportunities under Five-State Markov Capacity, Gilbert–Elliott burst-error, and Rayleigh block-fading channel models.
chk_setup.paper_quote: Using two phishing URL datasets, the framework is evaluated under Five-State Markov Capacity, Gilbert–Elliott burst-error, and Rayleigh block-fading models.

chk_primary_result.value: Under the Five-State Markov Capacity model, adaptive folding achieves 191.6 successful deliveries per MB, compared with 66.9 for the strongest compression baseline and 27.7 for the classical full filter.
chk_primary_result.paper_quote: Under the Five-State Markov Capacity model, adaptive folding achieves 191.6 successful deliveries per MB, compared with 66.9 for the strongest compression baseline and 27.7 for the classical full filter.

chk_secondary_result.value: Under the Five-State Markov Capacity model, adaptive folding reduces mean receiver age to 1.24 intervals, compared with 13.5 for the strongest compression baseline and 31.6 for the classical filter.
chk_secondary_result.paper_quote: Under the Five-State Markov Capacity model, adaptive folding reduces mean receiver age to 1.24 intervals, compared with 13.5 for the strongest compression baseline and 31.6 for the classical filter.

chk_baseline.value: Classical uncompressed filters, sparse uncompressed filters, and four lossless-compression baselines (gzip, zlib, bzip2, and LZMA).
chk_baseline.paper_quote: The sparse canonical bit array is compared with gzip [17], zlib [18], bzip2 [19], and LZMA [20].

chk_conclusion.value: Channel-aware folding improves communication efficiency and receiver freshness relative to complete-filter and lossless-compression baselines when communication opportunities vary substantially.
chk_conclusion.paper_quote: Channel-aware folding improves communication efficiency and receiver freshness relative to complete-filter and lossless-compression baselines when communication opportunities vary substantially.

chk_limitation.value: The controlled design uses fixed contents and cardinalities, which isolates channel-driven selection but does not establish generality across other workloads, cardinalities, occupancies, or changing contents.
chk_limitation.paper_quote: This isolates channel-driven selection but does not establish generality across other workloads, cardinalities, occupancies, or changing contents.
